tutorial.step1_body:
Flujo separates your money based on its purpose.

• Debit → money for spending
• Credit card → pending debt
• Investment → protected money
• Cash → physical money

The goal is not only to track movements. The goal is to know how much money you can actually use.
tutorial.step1_tip: Flujo works best when each account represents real money.
tutorial.step2_body:
Go to Settings → My accounts and add the accounts you use in daily life.

You can create:
• Debit accounts
• Cash accounts
• Credit accounts
• Investment accounts
tutorial.step2_tip: Example: “Main debit account”, “Credit card”, “Long-term investment”, “Wallet cash”.
tutorial.step3_title: Credit cards reduce your free money
tutorial.step3_body:
When you buy with a credit card, Flujo understands that the money is already committed.

Example:
• Total investments: $20,000
• Credit card debt: $5,000

→ Real free money: $15,000
tutorial.step3_tip: This helps you avoid spending money that you already need to pay your card.
tutorial.step4_body:
Use transfers to move money between your accounts without affecting your income or expenses.

Examples:
• Debit → investment
• Debit → cash
• Investment → credit card
tutorial.step4_tip: Transfers reorganize your money, they do not change your net worth.
tutorial.step5_body:
If your real balance does not match Flujo, use “Adjust balances”.

This syncs the app with reality without creating fake income or expenses.
tutorial.step5_tip: Example: bank balance $4,280 → Flujo $4,150 → adjust account.
tutorial.step6_body:
You can configure a maximum limit for your debit account.

If you go above it, Flujo will suggest moving the excess into investments to protect your money.
tutorial.step6_tip: Example: if your limit is $8,000 and you have $11,000, you can move $3,000 into investments.
tutorial.step7_body:
From now on, simply record:

• income
• expenses
• transfers

Flujo will automatically calculate:
• free money
• pending debt
• committed investments
• real spending capacity
tutorial.step7_tip: The goal is not to spend less. The goal is to know exactly which money you can safely use.
